  Home People Faculty & Staff Recruitment Faculty & Staff Recruitment Faculty positions in Computer Sciences Job summary: The Department of Computer Sciences at the University of Wisconsin-Madison has embarked on a multi-year effort to grow its faculty, enhance its strengths in many areas of computing, and extend its impact in interdisciplinary areas. As part of this endeavor, we invite highly qualified candidates in all areas of computer science to apply to positions at the assistant, associate, and full professor levels that will begin in August 2026. The successful candidates will advance the educational mission of the College of Letters & Science, that values, prioritizes, and actualizes evidence-based and student-centered teaching and (undergraduate student) mentoring. They will contribute to an inclusive, fair, and equitable environment that fosters engagement and a sense of belonging for faculty, staff, students, and members of the broader community.  Open positions for 2025-26 at this time are part of the Wisconsin Research, Innovation and Scholarly Excellence (RISE) Initiative. Further details on these positions can be accessed via the link below. Applications are sought in all areas of computer science. 
=== 20. UCLA ===
  Faculty Recruitment – Academic and Staff Positions Faculty Recruitment 2022-2023 Tenure Track Faculty Positions The Computer Science Department of the Henry Samueli School of Engineering and Applied Science at the University of California, Los Angeles, invites applications for tenure-track positions in all areas of Computer Science. Applications are also encouraged from distinguished candidates at senior levels. Candidates must have a Ph.D. to fulfill the basic qualification requirement. Quality is our key criterion for applicant selection. Applicants should have a strong commitment both to research and teaching and an outstanding record of research for their level of seniority. Salary is commensurate with education and experience. The University of California is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, age or protected veteran status. For the complete University of California nondiscrimination and affirmative action policy see: UC Nondiscrimination & Affirmative Action Policy .  cs-vnp">Tenure-Track Assistant or Associate Professor in Computer Science Northwestern University's Computer Science Department seeks outstanding candidates who are excited by the opportunity to help build the future of CS at a world-class university, both in core CS areas and collaboratively with other disciplines ( CS + X ). Northwestern is a leading R1 university comprising a number of highly-ranked schools that provide extraordinary opportunities for collaboration. Northwestern is located in beautiful Evanston, on the shores of Lake Michigan, just outside the diverse and culturally vibrant city of Chicago. Tenure-Track/Tenured: Assistant, Associate, and Full Professor - Computer Science and Engineering
Texas A&M University: College of Engineering: Computer Science & Engineering
Location

Open Date

Sep 10, 2026

Description

The Department of Computer Science and Engineering, College of Engineering at Texas A&M University, invites applications for ten full-time, tenure-track or tenure review upon hire, at all levels (Assistant, Associate, and Full Professor) with a nine-month academic appointment, and the possibility of an additional summer appointment contingent upon the need and availability of funds, beginning fall of 2027. Strong candidates in core, multi-disciplinary, or emerging areas of computing and AI are encouraged to apply. Particular areas of interest are (but not limited to) cybersecurity/privacy, database systems, formal methods, health computing, quantum computing, and responsible/human-centered AI. The department may hire multiple faculty in one or more of these areas to continue growing strong research clusters.

The successful applicant will be required to teach, advise, and mentor graduate and undergraduate students; develop and maintain an independent, externally funded research program with strong visibility through high-impact publications; participate in all aspects of the department’s activities; and serve the department, college, university, and/or profession, as applicable. Strong written and verbal communication skills are required. Applicants should visit http://www.cse.tamu.edu to review our academic and research programs.

The Department of Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) at Texas A&M is currently one of 15 departments in the College of Engineering. Many of the 57 tenured/tenure-track faculty and 28 teaching-focused faculty hold numerous national distinctions, including AAAI, ACM, IEEE, AAAS, SIAM Fellows, and ACM Distinguished Scientists and Engineers. The department has a strong and vibrant research program, with half the faculty having received NSF CAREER awards. CSE faculty have strong collaborations across Texas A&M in data science, health, cybersecurity, and national security, including through the Institute of Data Science, the Center for Remote Health Technologies and Systems, the Global Cyber Research Institute, the Cybersecurity Center, and the Bush Combat Development Complex. Texas A&M has recently invested $100 million in next-generation computing infrastructure through two major initiatives: VISION, a $45 million NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD with 760 NVIDIA H200 GPUs currently ranked as the fastest university supercomputer in the United States, and IGNITE, a $55 million AI and high-performance computing platform (arriving 2026/2027) with 320 liquid-cooled AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs to support large-scale research in national security, scientific discovery, and engineering. Together, these systems provide exceptional resources for cutting-edge AI and computing research. Our student population comprises nearly 1,700 undergraduate students (sophomores to seniors) and 700 graduate students. The department is housed in the Peterson Building, with airy modern offices, conference rooms, and lounges equipped with state-of-the-art A/V technology. More information about CSE is available at http://www.cse.tamu.edu.

Qualifications

Applicants must have earned a doctorate in computer science, computer engineering, or a closely related field. Candidates who have completed all Ph.D. requirements except the dissertation will be considered, provided they demonstrate clear progress towards completion.

Application Instructions

Applicants must submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae, personal statement (include philosophy and plans for research, teaching and service, as applicable), and a list of four contact references (include postal addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses) by applying for this specific position at https://apply.interfolio.com/192732. The review of applications will begin by December 1, 2026. Applications received after that date may be considered until positions are filled. It is anticipated that the appointments will begin in Fall 2027. 

For additional information regarding this position, please contact: k-waskom@tamu.edu

Application Process
This institution is using Interfolio's Faculty Search to conduct this search. Applicants to this position receive a free Dossier account and can send all application materials, including confidential letters of recommendation, free of charge.

Tenure-Track Faculty in Artificial Intelligence

 

Requisition Number:

 74736

Location:

 
Boulder, Colorado

 Boulder

 Faculty

 Full-Time

Date Posted:

 Job Summary
Job Summary

The Department of Computer Science at the University of Colorado (CU) Boulder seeks applications for two tenure-track Assistant Professor positions in artificial intelligence, broadly construed. We invite applications from all areas of AI. Areas of current interest include the following:

Foundations of machine learning
Multimodal models
Alignment and AI safety
Physical and embodied AI
Reasoning
Systems that make large models trainable and deployable

This list is illustrative rather than exhaustive. Applicants whose work falls outside these areas are encouraged to apply, including applicants whose work spans artificial intelligence and another discipline.

Artificial intelligence is a growth area for the campus and for the department. The Department of Computer Science offers a Bachelor of Science in Artificial Intelligence, and these two positions are part of a broader cluster of AI hiring. The department has recently made strategic investments in two AI Centers. Computing has been expanded alongside that: a Research Computing reinvestment has added NVIDIA H200 capacity, supported in part by the college and the department, with a share of it dedicated to teaching. AI research at CU Boulder extends beyond computer science into partners across the College of Engineering and Applied Science, cognitive science, information science, and collaborations with the federal laboratories along the Colorado Front Range. The Boulder area also supports a growing concentration of companies working in artificial intelligence and robotics.

CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.
 Who We Are
Who We Are

The University of Colorado Boulder (CU Boulder) is one of Colorado’s flagship public institutions and among the most research-active public universities in the country. The College of Engineering and Applied Science is the second largest school or college on the CU Boulder campus and boasts top-tier rankings for both its graduate and undergraduate engineering programs. Earning the 11th spot among public graduate programs and 17th nationwide for undergraduate engineering. Multiple specialty areas are also ranked within the top 20. Equally importantly, we are committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and academically excellent community. Our approximately 250 tenure-track, 120 instructional-track, and 30 research-track faculty serve more than 6,000 undergraduate students, 1,300 master’s students, and 850 PhD students. Our college has three core foci: (i) Research & Innovation, (ii) Education, and (iii) Inclusion. We believe that our college’s success requires faculty who actively work to create an inclusive culture within the college and are committed to the campus plan of creating and sustaining supportive campus environments.

To learn more about the College of Engineering and Applied Science please visit our website.

The Department of Computer Science is one of the largest departments within the College of Engineering and Applied Science at the University of Colorado Boulder (CU Boulder). The department is home to over 50 tenured and tenure-track faculty plus 25 instructional faculty and now includes about 2000 undergraduate and 500 graduate students. To learn more about the Department of Computer Science, please visit the department’s website.

 What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be
What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be
Successful candidates will be expected to engage in undergraduate and graduate teaching and mentoring; develop an externally funded research program in their technical area; contribute professional leadership and service to their unit, the college, and their professional community; and cultivate and contribute to the inclusive excellence of our academic community.
The typical distribution of work for this role is 40% teaching, 40% scholarly and creative work (research), and 20% leadership and service.
 What You Should Know
What You Should Know
The anticipated start date for these positions is Fall 2027; however, a later start date may be negotiated.
Only one application is necessary to be considered for both positions.
The University of Colorado Boulder has implemented a reference check program with respect to final candidates for tenured faculty appointments. The reference check program is intended to allow CU Boulder to collect and review information about a candidate's conduct at their current and previous institutions, specifically conduct related to sexual misconduct, harassment, and/or discrimination, before making hiring decisions. All final candidates for tenured faculty appointments are required to complete an Authorization to Release Information.
 What We Can Offer
What We Can Offer
The anticipated academic year salary range for this position at the Assistant Professor rank is $130,000 - $145,000.
A relocation stipend may be available within CEAS guidelines.
A recruitment incentive is available within Department guidelines.
CU offers a competitive 401(a) retirement plan, with employees contributing 5% of their annual eligible compensation and CU contributing 10% of their eligible compensation. This plan is standard for most faculty hires. For more information on CU's retirement benefits visit our website here.
In addition to a competitive salary, the University of Colorado Boulder offers a wide variety of other benefits and perks. Links to some of these are below. To forecast the value of your total compensation, check out our total compensation calculator. More information on some of our benefits and perks is available here: gender-neutral paid parental leave; housing down-payment assistance programs; dual-career & relocation resources; and teaching, research, and professional development.
 Benefits
Benefits

At the University of Colorado Boulder, we are committed to supporting the holistic health and well-being of our employees. Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical, dental, and retirement plans; generous paid time off; tuition assistance for you and your dependents; and an ECO Pass for local transit. As one of Boulder County’s largest employers, CU Boulder offers an inspiring academic community and access to world-class outdoor recreation. In fact, CU Boulder has been named one of Forbes' America's Best Large Employers, ranking #4 among large employers in Colorado and #28 among universities nationwide. Explore additional perks and programs through the CU Advantage program.

 Be Statements
Be Statements
Be inspired. Be game-changing. Be Boulder.
 What We Require
What We Require
Applicants must have earned a research doctorate in Computer Science or a related discipline before starting a tenure-track faculty appointment.
 What You Will Need
What You Will Need
A research agenda that can be pursued with external funding at CU Boulder.
Ability to teach at both the undergraduate and graduate level within the artificial intelligence curriculum.
Research interests that connect with existing work in the department or elsewhere on campus.
 What We Would Like You to Have
What We Would Like You to Have
A record of peer-reviewed publication in artificial intelligence or a related field, calibrated to career stage.
Experience teaching or mentoring students at the undergraduate or graduate level.
Experience collaborating across research groups, departments, or disciplines.
 Special Instructions
Special Instructions

To apply, please submit the following materials as individual PDF files:

Cover Letter: A one-page cover letter describing your interest in the position and summarizing your personal academic goals.
Resume/CV: A current curriculum vitae.
A Statement of Research Philosophy: A statement of your experience and plans for research and/or creative work that contributes to the body of knowledge in your field and provides broader benefits to education and society (3-4 pages).
A Statement of Teaching Philosophy: A statement of your experience and plans for teaching and mentoring a diverse student body (2-3 pages).
Leadership, Service and Community Contributions Statement: In this statement, describe your leadership and service experience, and demonstrated ability to contribute to a supportive campus community. Please provide details on your track record, calibrated to your career stage, that describe the specific role you played in these efforts. These could include, but are not limited to service on committees, outreach activities to broaden engagement in or with engineering, or serving on advisory boards or task forces contributing to policies or regulations. In addition, describe your plans to contribute to our campus plan to Create Supportive Environments, and the College of Engineering and Applied Science Strategic Vision (1-2 pages).
Names and contact information for three or more references: Contact information for at least three references who may be contacted as the search progresses. Please include names, job titles, phone numbers, and email addresses. Separately during the application process, you will be asked to provide the name and contact information for at least three references to submit a letter of recommendation to be considered along with your application materials. This is allowed to be the same individuals.
Applications will be accepted until the positions are filled, however for full consideration please apply by November 1, 2026.

Note: Application materials will not be accepted via email. For consideration, applications must be submitted through CU Boulder Jobs. Background checks will be conducted for all final applicants.



In compliance with the Colorado Job Application Fairness Act, in any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information.

Using **CSRankings** (USA, all areas), the top 50 institutions (encompassing 51 schools due to a tie at Rank 50 between UC Davis and the University of Minnesota) were pulled and systematically investigated school-by-school across their computer science department websites, engineering school portals, and university recruitment systems.

Because September marks the transition between the concluding review phases of the previous cycle and the formal posting of the upcoming cycle, universities generally fell into two categories:
1. **Active Postings Open Now**: 9 institutions have live, verified tenure-track/tenured openings in Computer Science, Machine Learning, AI, Systems, and related areas.
2. **Verified Closed / Preparing Upcoming Postings**: 42 institutions have concluded prior searches and explicitly indicate that upcoming cycle positions are pending (e.g., Georgia Tech noting "New positions will be posted soon!", UT Austin stating "The 2026-27 recruiting season will begin in October", or portals like MIT EECS, Columbia, UChicago, JHU, and Harvard showing their searches are closed to new applications).

## 5. Key Patterns & Strategic Recommendations

### A. Dominant Hiring Patterns
1. **Application Platform Standardization**:
   - **Interfolio Faculty Search** remains the dominant application system for private institutions and major state flagship engineering schools (CMU, UW, Texas A&M).
   - **UC Recruit (`apol-recruit` / `recruit.ap.uci.edu`)** is strictly unified across all University of California campuses (UCSD, UCI, Berkeley, UCLA, UCSB, UCD, UCSC).
   - Other institutions utilize internal enterprise platforms (Cornerstone OnDemand for UIUC, custom portals for Northwestern and Cornell).
2. **Hiring Cycle Phasing in September**:
   - The first wave of postings opens between **late August and mid-September** (CMU, UCSD, UCI, Texas A&M, CU Boulder all opened between Aug 10 and Sep 16).
   - Several major departments (e.g., UT Austin, Georgia Tech, UPenn, NYU Courant) explicitly schedule their 2026–2027 tenure-track postings to launch in **October**.
   - Review deadlines heavily cluster around **November 1 to December 1, 2026** (e.g., CU Boulder: Nov 1; Northwestern: Nov 6; UW: Nov 15; UCSD, UCI, Texas A&M: Dec 1; CMU: Dec 16).

### B. High-Demand Subfields
- **Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning**: Remains the single largest focus area across both open-area searches and dedicated cluster hires. CU Boulder is conducting targeted searches for two Assistant Professors specifically in Foundations of ML, Multimodal Models, and AI Safety; Northwestern has prioritized AI/ML across all areas.
- **Computer Systems & Architecture (Compilers / Systems for AI)**: Systems is explicitly prioritized in CMU's Computer Science Department, UC Irvine's dedicated JPF10340 search, and Northwestern's compiler/systems search.
- **Mass Scale Faculty Cluster Growth**: Texas A&M represents the largest single department cluster hire among the active postings, seeking **10 faculty members** across all ranks to support major computational infrastructure expansions (VISION DGX SuperPOD and IGNITE AI platforms).

### C. Strategic Recommendations
1. **Prioritize Early-Action Deadlines**: Prepare portfolio materials (Research Statement, Teaching Philosophy, 3–5 representative papers, and referee contact details) immediately to meet the **November 1 – November 15** review windows for CU Boulder, Northwestern, and the University of Washington.
2. **Monitor the October Wave**: Set a weekly review schedule during October for Georgia Tech, UT Austin, UPenn CIS, Michigan CSE, and Princeton DOF, which have scheduled their upcoming cycle openings to go live within the next two to four weeks.
3. **Target Systems & AI Convergence**: Candidates with research portfolios at the intersection of Systems and AI/ML (e.g., scalable ML systems, compilers, distributed AI infrastructure, and AI hardware co-design) are aligned with the explicit priority tracks at CMU, UC Irvine, Northwestern, and Texas A&M.
